items.text: A self-hosted Pulumi Cloud can be used by Terraform as a state backend.
A self-hosted Pulumi Cloud can be used by OpenTofu as a state backend.
Enabling the Terraform state backend on self-hosted Pulumi Cloud requires setting an environment variable (PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN) on the API service specifically.
The linked page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ (the Terraform state backend guide) exists.
The self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service supports an environment variable named `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN`.
`PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` sets the domain that serves the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud's Terraform-compatible API (e.g. `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud's Terraform-compatible API is disabled (default behavior).
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service does not register the Terraform-compatible API routes.
The Terraform-compatible API of self-hosted Pulumi Cloud is served by the same host that serves the Pulumi API (`PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`), so the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` DNS record should point at that host.
A separate domain for the Terraform-compatible API is not required: `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` may be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` and the Terraform-compatible API still works.
`PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` is the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service environment variable that specifies the domain serving the Pulumi API.

When using a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a Terraform/OpenTofu state backend, the Terraform or OpenTofu backend configuration uses the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the hostname in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
When using a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend, the `terraform login` / `tofu login` command is run against the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` hostname in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
When using a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend, the `TF_TOKEN_*` environment variable name is derived from the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
The Pulumi Terraform state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/) uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the hostname for the Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API.
Terraform provides a `terraform login` command and OpenTofu provides a `tofu login` command for authenticating to a remote backend host.
Terraform and OpenTofu read backend credentials from environment variables following the `TF_TOKEN_*` naming convention, where the suffix is derived from the backend hostname.
